name: Baruch (Jeremiah writes, son of Neriah)
title: The Prophet's Faithful Scribe
summary: Baruch was the son of Neriah and served as the personal scribe and secretary to the prophet Jeremiah. He wrote down Jeremiah's prophecies on scrolls, read them publicly, and remained faithful to the prophet through persecution and the fall of Jerusalem. He accompanied Jeremiah to Egypt after the Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Writing Jeremiah's Prophecies on a Scroll
keyEvents.description: Baruch wrote down all the words of the Lord that Jeremiah dictated to him on a scroll, after Jeremiah had been denied access to the temple.

keyEvents.title: Reading the Scroll in the Temple
keyEvents.description: Baruch read publicly from the scroll containing Jeremiah's prophecies in the house of the Lord on a day of fasting, so that all the people could hear God's word.

keyEvents.title: King Jehoiakim Burns the Scroll
keyEvents.description: When King Jehoiakim heard the contents of the scroll, he cut it into pieces and threw it into the fire. Baruch and Jeremiah had to hide.

keyEvents.title: Rewriting the Scroll
keyEvents.description: After the first scroll was burned, Jeremiah dictated all the words again to Baruch, who wrote them down once more with many additions.

keyEvents.title: Receiving a Personal Message from God
keyEvents.description: God gave Baruch a personal message through Jeremiah, warning him not to seek great things for himself, but promising that his life would be spared.

keyEvents.title: Following Jeremiah to Egypt
keyEvents.description: After the fall of Jerusalem, Baruch was taken with Jeremiah to Egypt by the remaining Judeans, despite God's warning against going there.
